chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibnfan ibn al-Sim al-Bajali, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the weak ones?' He said to me, resembling a state of panic: 'Have you left anyone who can be considered weak? And where are the weak ones? By Allah, the adolescent girls have carried this matter of yours to the adolescent girls in their chambers, and the water-carriers are discussing it in the streets of Medina.'

key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weak ones (of understanding or status)
key_terms.شَبِيهاً بِالْفَزِعِ: Resembling a state of panic or alarm

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq mean when he asked 'Where are the weak ones?' regarding the spread of knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the phenomenon of *al-mustad'afin* (the weak or limited in understanding) by noting that their specific teachings or status have become so ubiquitous that they are known even to adolescent girls in their private chambers and water-carriers in the streets. This reflects the Shia scholarly concept of the widespread dissemination of religious knowledge or specific jurisprudential rulings among the general populace, often leading to a dilution or popularization of deeper scholarly nuances.
